standard_prerequisites.name: The global hom complex admits a canonical map to the hom complex after base change, and the displayed map of the statement is obtained from it by adjointness
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the comparison map whose bijectivity is asserted.

standard_prerequisites.name: For an affine morphism, the pushforward of the pullback of an object is described by tensoring with the pushforward of the structure sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Rewrites the right hand side of the comparison as a derived Hom on the original scheme.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived sheaf Hom out of a perfect or pseudo-coherent complex has the positivity or finiteness properties required, and the internal Hom computation describes it in the tor independent case
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces both cases to the comparison statement for the derived sheaf Hom, which is where the two hypotheses enter.

core_obligations: Construct the comparison map: start from the canonical map of global hom complexes, view it as a map over the base ring by restriction of scalars, and use adjointness of restriction and extension of scalars to obtain the displayed map; it suffices to prove it is an isomorphism in the derived category of abelian groups (proof lines 5447-5455).
Rewrite the right hand side using the affine pullback-pushforward description, so that both sides involve the derived Hom of the same two objects on the source (proof lines 5456-5460).

Check that the derived sheaf Hom out of the perfect or pseudo-coherent complex has the required properties: in the first case it is perfect, in the second case it lies in the bounded below quasi-coherent category because the second object does and the tor dimension hypothesis controls the other argument (proof lines 5460-5472).

Apply the internal Hom computation that describes the derived sheaf Hom in the tor independent situation, which identifies both sides and gives the isomorphism in the two cases (proof lines 5473-5492).
proof_roadmap: Build the comparison map by adjointness (proof lines 5447-5455).
Rewrite the right hand side via pullback-pushforward (proof lines 5456-5460).
Control the derived sheaf Hom in the two cases (proof lines 5460-5472).
Apply the internal Hom computation to conclude (proof lines 5473-5492).
